reason: The cited lines show a dispatcher calling visibleHtmlTool.execute and a tool definition whose purpose is to return the HTML content of the current page, with options for cleaning/minifying it. They do not show arbitrary host code execution or any sending/writing of agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination. Returning current-page HTML establishes that the tool can bring web page content into the agent context, which is attacker-controllable in the general case, supporting UNTRUSTED. However, these lines do not establish that the current page is authenticated, local, intranet, or otherwise non-public, so SECRET is not settled by the cited lines alone.
